A.notes: A has a coherent signature: arches, route lines and merchant-house details carry the hotel story through every section without losing the booking task. Typography and spacing are calm and premium, and the room facts are very clear on both desktop and mobile. From the scroll strip, motion seems modest and mostly reveal-based; it supports the concept but does not add a strong narrative layer.

B.notes: B has the stronger central idea: the whole site is framed around thresholds, doors and the lane, and the hero is memorable. The scroll-frame strip shows a purposeful sequence of pinned narrative sections, and the reduced-motion fallback appears complete. But the normal full-page and mobile captures show very large blank spans and cramped/awkward content states, which hurts clarity, rooms-as-facts, and overall polish.

raw.why: A is the more complete and reliable response to the brief, with stronger clarity and craft, while B’s concept is excellent but its live layout behavior appears too fragile.
